summary: Anchor the forecast on the IOM Missing Migrants Project's annual Mediterranean death totals (around 2,400–2,500 per year) to establish a high-baseline reference class.
As of late February 2026, at least 606 deaths or missing persons have occurred, implying a non-negligible chance the total surpasses 1,000 before May if the pace persists into March–April.

question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 1,000 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before May 2026?
summary: Objections identify plausible downside risks to sustaining the early-2026 death pace (seasonality, policy/SAR changes, and route shifts).
The pace through February (606 deaths) implies some momentum, but two-month March–April demand ~394 deaths is uncertain and could be dampened.
The ensemble 0.85 already reflects optimism; given downside factors, a modest downward recalibration is warranted.
Despite downside, historical tolls and current momentum keep a non-negligible chance of crossing 1,000 by end-April, justifying a still-moderate-to-high probability.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and highlight real blockers that could slow momentum; none rely on physically implausible scenarios.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.85 to 0.78 to reflect downside risks while preserving the possibility implied by the early-year pace.
